notes: Batch exactly the orders you choose, release a reservation from a location, guided put-backs, bulk checkout counts the whole batch, kit notes, Prime pick faces

entries.title: Batch exactly the orders you choose, release a reservation from a location, guided put-backs, bulk checkout counts the whole batch, kit notes, Prime pick faces
items: Select exactly which orders go into a batch on the pick queue: tick rows, Shift-click to tick every row between, Select all shown (whatever the filters leave), type a number range (LUMI-000120 to LUMI-000160, or 120 to 160 inside one customer), or scan the barcode on each pick slip. The bar keeps a running “38 orders selected”.

Batch these builds carts from exactly that selection with the Pick in batches engine — up to twelve a cart, one packing type per cart, the most urgent first, and Keep each customer apart if you tick it. More than a cart's worth comes back as Cart 1 of N, each with Start.
Orders that can't go on a cart are never quietly dropped: being edited, on hold, already on a cart someone is picking, picking started, nothing reserved yet — each is listed with the reason.

Editing an order that's on a cart now takes it off the cart, and the cart carries on. The picker sees “LUMI-000142 was taken off this cart — it's being edited” and chooses Put back (onto the Put back list) or Keep with the order for anything already picked. The other orders keep their bin letters.
Once the edit is finished, the cart's note reads “it was edited by …” instead of “it's being edited”.
When the edit is finished the order is back in the pick queue for a new cart, and its order page shows “Taken off cart BATCH-000042 for an edit”.

Over the API: POST /api/v1/orders/pick-batch batches given orders, numbers or a range; /pick-batch/lookup finds orders by number or range; /orders/{id}/off-cart puts back or keeps an order's picked units.

Bulk checkout now checks stock for the batch as a whole. Before, each recipient was checked on their own, so 400 orders could pass when the shelf only covered 200 and the rest failed partway through. Now each recipient is counted against what the ones before it already need, the shortage is shown by product before anything is placed, and the brand's short-stock setting decides what happens.

Bulk checkout asks the brand's own checkout questions: once for every order in the batch (Order details, beside Ship how), or per recipient from a sheet column with the same name. Required questions are required here too — nothing is placed until each recipient is answered.
In the bulk check, a recipient stopped by a question or by stock now shows the units they asked for (not “0 units · $0.00”), and Fix the address only appears when it's the address that failed.
Renaming a checkout field no longer hides old answers: the field remembers its earlier names, so buyers and staff see orders answered before the rename under the new name.

Every part of a kit now carries a short note on the pick slip, the batch pick slip, the pick station and the pack bench: “Part of kit GIFT-HOST-SET (1 of 3) — also with: SOAP-LAV, CANDLE-01”. If one part is found and another isn't, the team knows exactly what else belongs with it.

The pick slip puts each kit back together above the table (Kits on this order): every part with its stop and location. The same kit twice on one order reads Kit 1 and Kit 2; three of a kit on one line says “1 per kit × 3”.

Short a kit part at the pick station and it says what else to pull: the rest of that kit, with each part's location and whether it's picked yet — leave it on the shelf and record it short, or Fix the stop to put it back. Shorts work as before: only what you record goes back to stock.

At the pack bench, a kit missing a part says which of its other parts to leave out of the box; they stay on the cart for the order's next shipment. The suggested first box already leaves them out, and Put everything left does too.
Kits made in Amphora are now marked exactly like kits that arrive from Propago — on slips, stations and the order page.
The packing slip in the box keeps it brief for the recipient: the kit's name heads its parts, and each reads “Included in Gift Host Set” — no codes, no locations.

Prime locations: mark a pick location Prime and it becomes a fixed home pick face that refills itself — refill when it drops to (min), fill up to (max). Only Prime locations get refill jobs or carry refill rules, and the nightly sizing only makes rules there.

Locations that aren't Prime are never refilled in place: when one runs empty, the SKU's next stock goes wherever putaway suggests, so its location can change as needed. Putaway never offers another SKU's Prime home.

Mark Prime on a location's page, in bulk on Stock → Locations (tick, then Mark Prime — with a Prime filter and column), or with the new prime column of the locations import and export. Watching a location that isn't Prime offers Make it Prime.
Stopping a location being Prime while rules watch it asks first: pause the rules (kept, resume later) or remove them.
Clearer numbers: rules now read “Refill when it drops to (min)” and “Fill up to (max)”, and a refill is proposed when a face reaches its min, not only once it's under it.
Upgrading changes nothing that works today: every location that already had a refill rule is marked Prime.
Pick stops show a Prime chip; Prime is reportable (Stock → Prime location) and on the API (POST /api/v1/bins/prime).

Release from a location: when a shelf is damaged, blocked, being counted, or the product just isn't there, release the order's reservation from that one location — on the order (Lines & allocation → Release from a location) or on the location itself (Reserved here). Choose Release and re-allocate elsewhere (reserved again, earliest expiry first, from other locations — backordered if nothing else covers it) or Release only (backordered). Every release records why and who.

Release everything reserved here: one button on a location re-allocates every order that would pick from it. Tick Keep this location out of allocation and its stock goes on Hold, so no order reserves it and no route sends anyone there until you press Use it again.
Units already picked can't be released — they're on the cart. Lower or remove the line and they become a put-back, as before. Orders someone is picking right now are left alone and listed.

Put back now says where to go: the location each item was picked from when it would still take it, otherwise the best other place (same lot or SKU there, the customer's area, an empty location) — never a location that's being counted or kept out. The list is in walk order, and Print the list gives you the same thing on paper.

Put back with the scanner (Scan → Put back): scan the location, scan the product, confirm how many. Put them somewhere else by scanning that location instead — it's checked against the same rules. Putting back part of it leaves the rest on the list. When the install allows offline scanning, a put-back made without a connection waits on the device and is checked again when it's sent.

entries.title: Required kit choices, kit-only parts, your own checkout fields, a polished storefront, rate card import, phones
items: Kits: a part can now be Required — the buyer must pick exactly one of the required parts in its group (a scent, a shade, a size). The portal asks “Scent — required, pick one” and won't add the kit to the cart until it's chosen; ordering without one, or with two, is refused by name. Required picks don't use up the buyer's-choice picks.

Sold: Only in a kit — for packaging and inserts that make no sense alone (SKU → Pricing & limits). They leave the portal's shop, an order for them on their own is refused, and kits holding them order as before. SKU import has a kit_only column; kit content imports take role required.

Your own checkout fields: in the Design studio (Cart & checkout), add as many questions as a brand needs — short or long text, dropdown, date, number, yes/no — each optional or required, with help text, and for everyone or only some user groups. Answers are checked on the server and saved on the order with its other custom fields; buyers see them on their order.

Import rate cards: one row per card, every fee in dollars, an optional price rise (date, percent, every N months), and the customer codes to put on it. Same name updates the card. From Billing → Rate cards or Setup → Import.
Staff logins are listed under Setup → Import too (Settings → Users → Invite several).
Phones: every screen now fits without sideways scrolling. The top bar keeps search, notices, the knowledge base and Sign out (as an icon); light/dark moved into the ☰ menu.

Portal storefront, polished: refined placeholders for products without photos, a home hero that shows your products, badges only when they mean something, category chips when there are few, a lighter header, quick add on the photo, quieter SKU codes, aligned prices and headings, better empty and loading states — and every page reworked for phones, with Add to cart pinned on product pages.
An import's check no longer sends its rolled-back audit entries to your security log copy (SIEM).

entries.title: Import anything from a spreadsheet
items: Setup → Import: every record you can load from a spreadsheet, in one place — and the same Import button on each record's own screen (Customers, a customer's Products, Categories, Carriers, Accounting, Portal people, Orders, Inbound, Returns, Pick replenish, Settings → Teams).

New imports: customers, shipping accounts, accounting units, categories, kit contents, price breaks, lots (with stop dates), orders, inbound shipments (ASNs), returns, pick-face refill rules, the portal address book, and teams.

Every import is guided the same way: get the template (Excel, with a sheet explaining every column, or CSV), upload it, check, then import. The check runs every row through the real rules and undoes it, so nothing is written until you press Import — and it says exactly how many will be added, updated or skipped, and names every problem by row and column.

Warnings before you finish: columns that will be ignored, the template's example rows left in, and rows with problems — which you confirm will be left out. Download just the rows to fix, with the reason on each.
Orders load through the same checks as one typed in, and an order reference already on file is skipped, so loading the same file twice never places anything twice.
Setup → Import templates is now Setup → Import.

entries.title: Portal design: brand guidelines in, eight new looks, finer options, announcements per group
items: Start from the brand guidelines: upload the PDF in the Design studio and Amphora finds its colours (HEX, RGB, CMYK, swatches — with their names and Pantone references) and typefaces, suggests which colour does what and the closest font pairing, and puts it on the preview for you to adjust.
Eight new looks — Luxe, Wellness, Sport, Heritage, Nordic, Kids, Tech and Festival — for twenty-four in all.

New options for every look: secondary, link, border, muted-text and badge colours; heading weight, capitals and letter spacing; shadows and line weight; a page background (dots, grid, lines, grain or a brand gradient); what sits behind product photos and how much room they get; button size.
Announcements for user groups: a bar just for the East stores, another for the field team — everyone else sees the usual one.

entries.title: Safe order edits, bulk changes for everything, stop dates, teams
items: Editing an order on the floor is safe: once it's being picked or packed, changes happen inside an edit that stops picking first. The picker's screen says stop, picks and packing wait, and the order leaves the pick queue until you press Done with a comment saying what changed and why.

Edited orders say so everywhere — the order page, the Orders list, the pick queue, the scanner and the pick slip — with who, when and the reason. Every order also has Internal comments the client never sees.

Cycle counts hold still: while a SKU, client, zone or location is being counted, it can't be picked, moved or received — orders that need it wait in the pick queue — until counting is done or a manager releases the lock. SKUs with nothing on hand, or never received, can now be counted too, with + Add a find for what turns up.

Draft SKUs, finished by the team that knows the client: rename a draft to its real code, or merge it into the SKU it really is — its stock moves lot for lot, its barcodes and links follow. Old placards keep scanning and the scan says the code changed, who changed it and when; the SKU page lists the placards to reprint.

Bulk changes, redone: Change these orders opens one plain step at a time, and now covers everything an order's edit can change — add, change, swap or take off products; carrier, ship date, ship-to address, building, signature, partial shipments, carrier account; reference, tag, notes and custom fields. Orders on the floor are left alone, with the reason.
Rush on and off, in bulk or on one order (Fix order): rush moves the ship-by to the rush promise and bills the fee; not rush credits the fee and puts the normal ship-by back.

Undo a bulk change: each order goes back to its own previous values — its own address, carrier, lines. On the Done step, or later under Undo a recent bulk change; orders that moved on since are left alone and named.

Teams (Settings → Teams): named groups of staff — Receiving, Solutions, Fulfillment, Inventory — each choosing what it hears about. Notices land on a new bell at the top of every screen and by email (to each member, a team inbox, or bell only).
Draft SKUs created at receiving, or by a Propago order naming an unknown part, now tell the team that sets SKUs up. Lots that stop being used within 30 days are sent each morning.

Stop using stock N days before its expiry: per SKU (SKU → Compliance), for every product of a brand (Customer → Overview), or per lot with its own date (the SKU's Inventory tab). From that day the lot reads Stopped — no new order reserves it, and the portal and Available stop counting it.
A lot can also keep being used until it expires, overriding the rule, with a reason kept on the lot and in the audit trail.
Inventory has a Stopped column; Reports → Expiring lots lists lots that stop inside the window, with a Stops column (also in its CSV and scheduled email).
Customer → Overview now shows the brand's Minimum life left when it ships, which already skipped lots that would arrive with too little life but had nowhere to be set.
Fixed: Reports → Expiring lots counted every move and status change as more stock, so Units on hand could read too high; and its scheduled email showed no units.

entries.title: Kit groups and order; pick several values in report filters
items: Kit contents can sit under group headings (Packaging, Products, Add-ons) and in the order you choose. Drag a part by its handle, drag a group by its heading, or use the arrows.

The portal shows the kit the same way: a heading per group, locked parts and the buyer’s picks under their own heading. The cart, checkout and the order’s packing slip list the contents in the kit’s order.
Groups are for reading only: quantities, the pick count, picking, stock and billing don't change. Kits with no groups look as they did.

Reports: is any of is a multi-select on every text field — tick the statuses, carriers, customers or cities you want from the values your data really holds. Fixed: typing a comma in that box used to vanish, so you could only ever enter one value. Text fields also get is none of.

Reports: the full ship-to address. Orders → Shipping now has company, contact, address 1, 2 and 3, phone, email and residential next to city, state, postcode and country; bill-to is under More · Orders, and every address Amphora stores as one record (user group home address, saved portal addresses) is offered part by part.

entries.title: Test worlds: switching on Propago (or any connection) works
items: Fixed: in a test world, ticking Propago, Email, Shopify or any other connection under Settings → Worlds said “Invalid input” and stayed off. Each switches on and off on its own now.
A connection that's off in a test world now says where to switch it on: “…switch it on in this world under Settings → Worlds.”

entries.title: Company sign-in works behind an HTTPS proxy again
items: Fixed: behind an HTTPS proxy, company and portal sign-in (SAML, OIDC) showed http:// links and refused sign-ins since 1.48.0 — Amphora only trusts a proxy's forwarded headers from AMPHORA_TRUSTED_PROXIES, so it couldn't tell the request was https.

Settings → General → Web address: the address people reach Amphora at (https://wms.yourcompany.com). Sign-on, portal sign-on, the portal API docs, Shopify and email links are all built on it, whatever the proxy sends. The sign-in setup warns when its links start with http://.

entries.title: Shipping accounts, Location in reports, SKU status in the report builder, whole product photos
items: Reports say Location, not Bin: the report builder's Location and Location type (and From / To location on the ledger), the stock and license plate exports' location column, the ledger export's from_location and to_location, and the count, move and kitting screens — a location is a bin or a pallet position. The stock import template's column is location; files with the old bin column still import.

Every column, in reports: each report in Build a report now offers every column of its records and of everything it reaches (under More · <table>), and every other table is a report of its own under All tables — locations, zones, lots, license plates, returns, cycle counts, transfers, work orders, mailings and more, about 100 in all. Secrets and raw data are never included; these extra columns and tables are for staff and can't be given to a brand.
Inventory → Stock tags a SKU that isn't live — Draft (still being set up) or Discontinued (retired) — and can be filtered by SKU status, so stock of a product nobody can order stands out.
SKU status (draft, active, discontinued) can be a column or a filter in the report builder — on Stock on hand, the ledger, order lines, inbound, billable events and print pieces.

Fixed: a product's main photo on the client store's product page cropped square photos (the wide frame cut off their top and bottom). The whole photo now always shows, and the SKU's Images card shows each image whole too.

Customers → the customer → Carriers → Shipping accounts lists the customer's own carrier accounts, each switched on or off, with how it's billed: as a third party (the account isn't the recipient's — billed at its own billing ZIP) or as the receiver. Each shows who bills it and how many labels it has billed.

Which account orders bill, one setting at a time: only when the order names one, one account for the whole portal, or each user group its own. If both were ever set, the user group's account wins. An account the order itself names (a Propago order, the API) always comes first.
UPS and FedEx labels bill a third-party account properly now, at the account's own billing ZIP — before, every customer account was billed as the receiver.

Accounts that change: an order naming an account that isn't on the list adds it switched off, marked Needs review, and its labels wait until someone adds the billing ZIP and switches it on. A switched-off account stops the label with the reason.

entries.title: Pick in batches: carts by shortest walk, zone, rush, carrier & service, or customer
items: The pick queue builds carts for you, five ways: Shortest walk (orders that save real walking together), Zone (one zone per cart, orders needing two zones kept whole), Rush & due (rush carts first, all rush), Carrier & service (UPS Ground and UPS 2nd Day Air on their own carts, each carrier with its services as rows) and Customer. Keep each customer apart works with all of them.

Each group is one row: “67 orders → 6 carts”, Cart 1 of 6 with its stops and how much less walking it is, and Start cart 1. See all carts lists the rest. Carts hold up to 12 orders, never mix packing types, and are built from the whole queue — fast at thousands of orders.
The filters (date, status, customer, zone, packing and the new Carrier filter) now sit on Orders to pick, the list they narrow. Ticking orders to build your own cart works as before.
The handheld pick screen has the same Pick in batches, folded into one line above the scanner.

entries.title: File drops: placards, slips and print files straight to Switch — by SFTP, S3 or a folder
items: Settings → File drops writes documents as the work happens to a folder, an SFTP server or an S3 bucket, for Enfocus Switch (or any hot folder) to route to the right printer and tray. Owners and admins set it up; Add and test tries each destination straight away.

Tick what drops, each with its own settings: placards when stock lands in a location (receiving, moves — or a license plate's placard, once, instead of one per SKU); pick slips when an order is ready to pick or picking starts, in pick-queue order (rush first), plus the batch's slip when a batch pick opens; pack slips when packing starts or the order is packed; print-ready PDFs for print-on-demand and direct mail jobs when they're ready or go to press; scheduled reports as they're emailed.

File names and folders are patterns — {seq}, {order}, {customer}, {carrier}, {location}, {sku}… — with an example under each drop. A job ticket (XML) can land beside each file with the customer, order, carrier, rush, ship-by and quantity, for Switch to route on.

Files arrive whole (written then renamed into place), within about five seconds. If a destination can't be reached, files wait and try again with the reason shown; Sent lists every file, with Send again. SFTP servers are pinned to the key seen on the first test.
A drop starts from the moment it's switched on — nothing that already happened is sent. In a test world, file drops stay off unless switched on there.
